assignmentDisclaimer: Assignment identifies the responsible human reviewer; it is not approval, activation, or authorization to acquire source data.

observedFacts: The pilot registry identifies the FDA website as the first-party origin for regulatory, safety-alert, drug-approval, and consumer-warning material.
openFDA documents Drugs@FDA, NDC, drug-label, and substance endpoints with separate dataset-specific fields and limitations.
openFDA authentication documentation states a 240-request-per-minute limit; the documented daily limit is 1,000 requests without an API key and 120,000 requests with an API key.
openFDA terms apply CC0 to openFDA data except content such as GMDN data that carries separate restrictions, including a redistribution restriction.
FDA website policy distinguishes federal material from third-party material that may carry separate copyright or trademark restrictions.
Every future evidence item must identify its specific FDA page, dataset record, label, or communication.

prohibitedUses: All acquisition, storage, transformation, redistribution, and canonical use until human legal approval.
redistributionConstraints: No source content may be redistributed until the applicable terms and content-specific restrictions are reviewed.

acquisition.accessNotes: API and bulk capability are technical observations only; select an exact endpoint and approve its terms before retrieval.

limitations: A regulator page must not be generalized beyond the cited product, communication, date, and jurisdiction.
Regulatory evidence is observational source material until claim-level human review.

refresh.proposedCadence: Daily checks for watched communications and a weekly baseline review.

remediation.correctionProcedure: Quarantine affected claims, preserve the superseded source pointer, and require evidence-reviewer approval before replacement.
remediation.retractionProcedure: Block affected claims when the cited FDA item is withdrawn, superseded, or materially changed.
remediation.removalProcedure: Remove stored source content and derived display material when required by legal or security review while retaining a non-content audit record.

proposedPermittedContent: Source URLs, page identifiers, publication or update dates, and claim-specific excerpts approved by legal review.
restrictedContent: Unreviewed bulk content, uncited summaries, personalized medical guidance, and claims outside the cited communication.

unresolvedQuestions: Which exact FDA APIs, datasets, and web content classes are approved for the first acquisition phase?
What terms, attribution, rate limits, and redistribution rules apply to each selected endpoint?
What retention period is approved for retrieved source snapshots?

observedFacts: The pilot registry identifies PubChem as a first-party NCBI source for compound identity and mechanism-oriented metadata.
PubChem documents programmatic access and separate downloadable archives for higher-volume acquisition.

PubChem dynamic throttling documentation lists limits of no more than five requests per second, 400 requests per minute, and 300 seconds of server processing time per minute; throttled requests can return HTTP 503.
PubChem records aggregate content from identified data contributors, and the data-sources documentation exposes contributor-specific attribution and license information.
PubChem publishes citation guidance for the service and its records.
The registered boundary does not treat PubChem as evidence of clinical efficacy, dosing, contraindications, monitoring, or regulatory truth.

prohibitedUses: All acquisition, storage, transformation, redistribution, and canonical use until human legal approval.
redistributionConstraints: No compound record or derived dataset may be redistributed until record-level attribution and upstream-source constraints are reviewed.

acquisition.accessNotes: API and bulk capability are technical observations only; approve endpoint, fields, attribution, and rate policy before retrieval.

limitations: Compound metadata does not establish clinical efficacy, dosing, contraindications, monitoring, or regulatory status.
Upstream depositor and linked-record provenance must remain distinguishable from PubChem aggregation.

refresh.proposedCadence: Monthly baseline refresh and manual refresh for an actively reviewed compound.

remediation.correctionProcedure: Quarantine the affected identity or mechanism fields and re-resolve them against the cited PubChem record.
remediation.retractionProcedure: Block derived fields when the cited record or upstream depositor evidence is withdrawn or materially changed.
remediation.removalProcedure: Remove stored record content and derived display material when required while retaining identifiers and a non-content audit record.

proposedPermittedContent: Stable compound identifiers, names, structures, source URLs, update dates, and reviewed mechanism metadata.
restrictedContent: Unreviewed linked-source text, clinical conclusions, dosing content, and bulk redistribution.

unresolvedQuestions: Which PubChem fields and upstream deposit sources may BioStack store and display?
What attribution and derived-dataset restrictions apply to the selected record fields?
What request-rate and bulk-download controls are required?

observedFacts: The pilot registry identifies PubMed as the first-party NLM index for papers, reviews, and human and preclinical studies.
NCBI E-utilities guidance limits clients to three requests per second without an API key and ten requests per second with an API key.
NLM publishes PubMed baseline and update-file download routes separately from interactive search and E-utilities.
NLM download guidance states that some PubMed records contain copyrighted abstracts and that users are responsible for determining and complying with applicable rights.
Index presence is not an evidence-quality determination; individual papers require extraction and grading.

prohibitedUses: All acquisition, storage, transformation, redistribution, and canonical use until human legal approval.
redistributionConstraints: Citation metadata, abstracts, and linked full text must remain separate and follow their respective rights boundaries.

acquisition.accessNotes: API capability is a technical observation only; approve exact metadata, abstract, and linked-content boundaries before retrieval.

limitations: Indexing does not establish study quality, applicability, or clinical certainty.
Every promoted claim requires claim-level linkage to the underlying publication and evidence grading.

refresh.proposedCadence: Daily metadata refresh for active topics and a monthly baseline re-query.

remediation.correctionProcedure: Quarantine affected claims, preserve citation lineage, and re-grade the underlying publication.
remediation.retractionProcedure: Block claims linked to retracted or materially corrected publications until evidence review is completed.
remediation.removalProcedure: Remove stored text that lacks approved rights while retaining permitted citation metadata and audit lineage.

proposedPermittedContent: Citation identifiers, bibliographic metadata, query provenance, and rights-approved abstract fields.
restrictedContent: Publisher full text without source-specific authorization, ungraded conclusions, and personalized medical guidance.

unresolvedQuestions: Which citation, abstract, and linked-full-text fields are approved for storage and display?
What API identification, request-rate, caching, and retention controls are required?
How will retraction and correction notices invalidate downstream claims?

observedFacts: The pilot registry identifies ClinicalTrials.gov as the first-party NLM registry for trials, emerging research, and drug development.
ClinicalTrials.gov documents a versioned API v2, a machine-readable version endpoint, migration guidance, and study-record download methods.
The reviewed API and terms pages do not publish a numeric requests-per-second quota; an operational rate limit therefore remains unresolved.
ClinicalTrials.gov states that study information is submitted by study sponsors and investigators and is not reviewed or approved by the U.S. government.
Trial registration does not prove efficacy or safety; posted results require separate review.

prohibitedUses: All acquisition, storage, transformation, redistribution, and canonical use until human legal approval.
redistributionConstraints: Registry data must remain labeled as registry data and must not be represented as peer-reviewed outcome evidence.

acquisition.accessNotes: API and bulk capability are technical observations only; approve exact endpoints, fields, and update handling before retrieval.

limitations: Registration and recruitment status do not establish efficacy, safety, or completion.
Outcome claims require separate publication evidence and evidence grading.

refresh.proposedCadence: Weekly refresh for watched studies and a monthly baseline refresh.

remediation.correctionProcedure: Quarantine affected trial fields and refresh from the cited NCT record before review.
remediation.retractionProcedure: Block derived claims when a study is withdrawn, terminated, or materially corrected until evidence review.
remediation.removalProcedure: Remove disallowed stored fields while retaining the NCT identifier, allowed provenance, and audit lineage.

proposedPermittedContent: NCT identifiers, study status, phase, interventions, conditions, update dates, and source URLs.
restrictedContent: Efficacy conclusions inferred from registration, unstated outcome claims, and personalized medical guidance.

unresolvedQuestions: Which registry fields are approved for storage, display, and export?
What update cadence and change-detection policy will prevent stale study status?
How will linked publications be resolved and reviewed as separate evidence sources?

observedFacts: The pilot registry identifies DailyMed as the first-party NLM source for U.S. drug labels.
DailyMed documents web-service endpoints and separate bulk Structured Product Label download resources.
DailyMed describes its content as FDA-submitted labeling currently in use, while retaining product- and version-specific identifiers.
The reviewed DailyMed web-service and bulk-download pages do not document an authentication requirement or numeric requests-per-second quota.
NLM website policy distinguishes U.S. government material from third-party content that may carry separate rights.
The registered boundary is product-specific and does not validate compounded or research-product claims.

prohibitedUses: All acquisition, storage, transformation, redistribution, and canonical use until human legal approval.
redistributionConstraints: Every displayed field must remain associated with its exact SPL set ID, label version, product, and effective date.

acquisition.accessNotes: API and bulk capability are technical observations only; approve label fields, attribution, update handling, and retention before retrieval.

limitations: Label evidence is specific to the labeled product, version, formulation, route, and jurisdiction.
Label content must not be converted into personalized prescribing or treatment guidance.

refresh.proposedCadence: Weekly label refresh and an immediate refresh for watched products after an observed label update.

remediation.correctionProcedure: Quarantine affected label fields and replace them only from the exact updated SPL record after review.
remediation.retractionProcedure: Block superseded label content when a newer effective version changes the cited section.
remediation.removalProcedure: Remove disallowed stored label content while retaining identifiers, version lineage, and a non-content audit record.

proposedPermittedContent: SPL identifiers, NDCs, label versions, effective dates, section identifiers, and rights-approved section content.
restrictedContent: Cross-product generalizations, compounded-product claims, personalized prescribing, and uncited label text.

unresolvedQuestions: Which label sections may BioStack store, quote, display, and export?
What attribution and update requirements apply to displayed SPL content?
How will label supersession invalidate previously extracted fields?

sources.sourceName: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Fact Sheets

observedFacts: The pilot registry identifies NIH ODS fact sheets as a first-party NIH source for vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements.
ODS publishes a first-party API surface and a direct contact route for questions about ODS information and reuse.
ODS FAQ guidance states that ODS-authored information is in the public domain and may be reproduced without permission when it is kept unchanged and ODS is acknowledged.
ODS guidance distinguishes third-party material, including images or other content carrying separate copyright, from ODS-authored public-domain text.
The registered boundary treats ODS as a medical summary rather than a product label.

prohibitedUses: All acquisition, storage, transformation, redistribution, and canonical use until human legal approval.
redistributionConstraints: Source text and derived summaries may not be stored or redistributed until page-level reuse and attribution requirements are reviewed.

acquisition.accessNotes: ODS publishes an API surface, but the pilot registry records no approved API route; approve its exact scope, terms, robots treatment, and operational limits before retrieval.

limitations: ODS is not a product label and cannot independently support safety-critical or product-specific dosing claims.
Consumer fact-sheet summaries must remain distinguishable from underlying studies and labels.

refresh.proposedCadence: Monthly update check and manual refresh when the source records a page update.

remediation.correctionProcedure: Quarantine affected summary fields and re-review the exact updated page and section.
remediation.retractionProcedure: Block derived claims when a fact sheet or cited section is removed or materially changed.
remediation.removalProcedure: Remove disallowed stored page content while retaining permitted URL, update-date, and audit metadata.

proposedPermittedContent: Page URLs, titles, section identifiers, update dates, and rights-approved claim-specific excerpts.
restrictedContent: Unreviewed page copies, individualized dosing, treatment plans, and product-label assertions.

unresolvedQuestions: Does the ODS API cover the fact-sheet fields selected for BioStack, and should the pilot registry's technical capability metadata be updated after review?
What page-reuse, quotation, attribution, and caching terms apply?
Is automated retrieval permitted, and under what robots and rate constraints?
Which claims require additional label or primary-literature evidence before promotion?

sources.sourceName: NIH National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health

observedFacts: The pilot registry identifies NCCIH as a first-party NIH source for supplements, sleep, botanicals, and consumer-health summaries.
The reviewed NCCIH policy and contact pages do not document a public data API; acquisition method and rate controls therefore remain unresolved.
NCCIH policy states that most NCCIH-authored website text is public domain, while photographs, illustrations, and other third-party material may be copyrighted.
NCCIH provides a first-party contact route for permission and policy questions.
The registered boundary does not treat NCCIH summaries as a substitute for labels or clinical guidelines for safety-critical fields.

prohibitedUses: All acquisition, storage, transformation, redistribution, and canonical use until human legal approval.
redistributionConstraints: Source text and derived summaries may not be stored or redistributed until page-level reuse and attribution requirements are reviewed.

acquisition.accessNotes: The registered source has no approved API or bulk route; any future page retrieval requires explicit legal, robots, and operational review.

limitations: NCCIH consumer summaries cannot independently support product-specific dosing, regulatory, or safety-critical claims.
Summary statements must remain linked to the exact page, section, and update date.

refresh.proposedCadence: Monthly update check and manual refresh when the source records a page update.

remediation.correctionProcedure: Quarantine affected summary fields and re-review the exact updated page and section.
remediation.retractionProcedure: Block derived claims when a source page or cited section is removed or materially changed.
remediation.removalProcedure: Remove disallowed stored page content while retaining permitted URL, update-date, and audit metadata.

proposedPermittedContent: Page URLs, titles, section identifiers, update dates, and rights-approved claim-specific excerpts.
restrictedContent: Unreviewed page copies, personalized treatment guidance, product-label assertions, and regulatory conclusions.

unresolvedQuestions: What page-reuse, quotation, attribution, and caching terms apply?
Is automated retrieval permitted, and under what robots and rate constraints?
Which claims require separate label, guideline, or primary-literature evidence before promotion?
